description: PF5 on an identifier SHORTER than its declared PIC X(08) - the STRING ... DELIMITED BY SPACE operand, and the only case in parity/COUSR03C that can observe it. DELETE-USER-INFO at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:174-192 takes the fourth arm of the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :108-130, the WHEN DFHPF5 of :121-122; USRIDINI is non-blank so the EVALUATE TRUE at :176-186 falls to WHEN OTHER, which moves -1 into USRIDINL and CONTINUEs without raising the error flag. The single IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at :188 then wraps BOTH the read and the delete - there is NO second guard between them, which is the structural fact case10, case13 and case15 exploit and which is modelled here as it is written rather than as a guard that does not exist. READ-USER-SEC-FILE at :267-300 issues EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE, whose NORMAL arm at :281-286 executes a dead CONTINUE at :282 - a no-op artifact preserved, not tidied - then moves the confirmation prompt and DFHNEUTR and sends (send 1 of 2). DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE at :302-336 then issues EXEC CICS DELETE at :307-311 with DATASET, RESP and RESP2 and NO RIDFLD: it removes the record the preceding read-for-update left the task HOLDING, not a record located by key, so the repository contract asserted here is readForUpdate then deleteHeld and never a delete-by-key - a translation reading delete(userId) would pass a naive test yet silently succeed where the COBOL cannot. The NORMAL arm at :314-322 then runs four steps whose ORDER is the assertion: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :315 (:349-356) blanks USRIDINI, FNAMEI, LNAMEI, USRTYPEI and WS-MESSAGE and re-cursors USRIDINL, which is why all four data items of the last send are BLANK; the redundant MOVE SPACES at :316 is left in place; DFHGREEN goes to ERRMSGC at :317; and only THEN does the STRING at :318-321 compose the confirmation - from a SEC-USER-DATA that INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS deliberately does not touch, which is how the identifier survives into a message painted over an emptied screen. THE POINT OF THIS CASE: SEC-USR-ID is PIC X(08) and the middle STRING operand is DELIMITED BY SPACE, not BY SIZE, so the eight-byte field holding 'AB      ' contributes exactly TWO characters and the sentence reads 'User AB has been deleted ...'. All ten identifiers in app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 occupy the full eight characters, which makes the two delimiters indistinguishable on every one of them; this case therefore seeds an ELEVENTH row whose key is short, and it is the only row seeded here that the JCL does not carry. A concatenation of the raw field would read 'User AB       has been deleted ...' and diverge on every short identifier, so the eleventh row is what turns BY SPACE versus BY SIZE from an unverifiable reading into a failing diff. SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN at :213-225 repaints all six header items through POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :243-262 on BOTH sends and moves the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE into the 78-byte ERRMSGO at :217, an 80-to-78 RIGHT truncation pinned on both channels at both widths so the direction is assertable. The invocation ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU03') COMMAREA of :134-137, so the termination is RETURN_TRANSID and not an XCTL, and the commarea travels in the payload: no server-side session state, no COMMAREA held on the server, in keeping with the pseudo-conversational contract. The state is REENTER, yet the path SUCCEEDS, so no DFHRED-plus-asterisk highlight appears anywhere - that highlight is both REENTER-only and error-only, and COUSR03C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY but sets its attributes inline. Ten rows survive at indices 0 to 9 and the AB row is gone; each survivor is pinned both field by field, so the named SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) is asserted BY NAME as 23 spaces, and as its whole 80-byte image, so the total width is asserted too and an omitted FILLER would collapse the record to 57 and fail loudly. SEC-USR-PWD holds the literal PASSWORD in every seeded and every asserted record because app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl does and the eighty bytes cannot be asserted without it: plaintext credentials are an INHERITED property of the legacy design, not a choice made here - COSGN00C compares that span in plaintext, this screen has no password field among its eleven xxxI items and never paints or reads the span, and no hashing, token or filter chain is introduced because that would change observable behaviour. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key USRSEC, never by a dataset name; app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD declares DELETE(YES) on FILE(USRSEC), which is what authorises this path. PROVENANCE: every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the sources named above and is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL - running it is empirically impossible in this environment (no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler's indexed-file handler is disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository), the documented eight-blocker deviation escalated as risk R-A; it changes the provenance of the expected values and nothing else. Derived from app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:106-137, :174-192, :213-225, :232-238, :243-262, :267-300, :302-336 and :349-356, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 (8+20+20+8+1 = 57, plus SEC-USR-FILLER's 23 = 80), app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY (COUSR3AO REDEFINES COUSR3AI, eleven xxxI items, no password item), app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy with app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:50-58, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for the two 40-character titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header clock, and the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose 57-character width against the LRECL=80,RECFM=FB of :48 and the RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) of :64-66 is exactly what the declared 57-to-80 normalisation supplies. The ten-row seed block, the pinned 2022-07-19T23:12:35 clock, the six record field names and that normalisation are case01's conventions, matched here byte for byte.
